short_case_summary: AARO's Puerto Rico Object Case Resolution (Document 25-P-0553, dated 20 March 2025; published on aaro.mil UAP Case Resolution Reports listing 2026-06-06) — a Tier-1 conventional-explanation update to the existing 2013 Aguadilla case (PRUAP-0422 + PRUAP-0423 in master ledger). AARO assesses with HIGH CONFIDENCE that the objects did NOT exhibit anomalous behavior or transmedium capabilities; with MODERATE CONFIDENCE that the objects were a pair of sky lanterns. Specific physics findings: (1) STK reconstruction showed objects drifted at 3.6 m/s (8 mph) consistent with recorded wind 4.4 m/s (9.8 mph) from E/NE; (2) thermal crossover within 2-hour post-sunset window (sunset 19:48 AST, encounter 21:22 AST) explains 'water entry' as IR signature loss when ocean came into background; (3) two objects (not one splitting) confirmed by pixel analysis showing separation at 00:29, 00:40, 00:47; (4) objects <1m diameter; (5) local hospitality vendors confirmed sky-lantern releases common during celebrations in the area. AARO explicitly REJECTED marine-birds hypothesis (no wing-flap signature in IR) and mylar-balloons hypothesis (IR cannot detect reflected moonlight).
source_name: AARO (DoD All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office), case 25-P-0553, March 20, 2025
conventional_explanation_check: Government Tier-1 source assesses: pair of sky lanterns (moderate confidence). Wind-driven motion at 8 mph, thermal-crossover-induced apparent water entry, motion-parallax-induced apparent high speed
why_it_counts: Tier-1 government source resolves a famous PR UAP case to a prosaic explanation. Updates the ledger's PRUAP-0422 + PRUAP-0423 with specific sky-lantern attribution + thermal-crossover physics.
